extracted.intended_audience: faculty-led multidisciplinary research teams preparing FY25 MURI white papers and proposals for AFOSR/ARO/ONR
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and preparing white papers/full proposals in response to FY25 MURI topic descriptions; aligning project objectives, scope, team composition, methods, and resources to the solicitation's stated expectations and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary expertise (energy/information topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The envisioned research would require multidisciplinary expertise from among biology, neuroscience, cellular neurobiology, biophysics, biochemistry, and information theory (likely from computer science and/or mathematics) to collect relevant experimental data ... and potentially develop appropriate theoretical models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should assemble teams with the listed disciplines and be prepared to collect experimental data using techniques such as electrophysiology, optical I/O methods, chemical analyses, and/or genetics and to develop theoretical models as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider energetic requirements across scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers should consider energetic requirements for information processing across the spectrum from cellular or subcellular levels to integrated sensory, cognitive, and motor systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address energy/information relationships at appropriate scales for the posed research questions; justify chosen scale(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify definition and measures of information
rubrics_metrics.description: There are multiple ways to define and quantify information. Proposers should specify their definition and associated measure(s) based on appropriateness for their research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state and justify the information-theoretic definitions and metrics to be used and why they are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with topic Objective (energy/information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: support investigations of relationships between energy consumption and information processing in biological organisms with a goal of identifying strategies that could have implications for human and computer performance in energy-constrained environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must address the stated objective and describe how planned work will identify strategies or insights relevant to energy-constrained information processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: graceful-degradation info-processing strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Information processing strategies observed in biological organisms that trade reduced energy consumption or metabolic demands with graceful degradations in computation and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should identify, characterize, or model such strategies and their tradeoffs between energy savings and degraded precision/behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: cost per information bit
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors impacting the metabolic/energetic cost of an information bit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should quantify or model contributors to energetic cost per bit and experimentally or theoretically evaluate those factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: biophysically-realistic model predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictions from biophysically-realistic models of information processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and test models that make testable predictions about energy-information relationships grounded in biophysics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: implications for human cognition under caloric restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Implications for human perceptual and cognitive performance under moderate to severe caloric restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include translational work or modeling that links observed biological strategies to human perceptual/cognitive outcomes when energy availability is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: information-theory strategies for artificial systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Information theory-based computational strategies for artificial systems in energy-constrained conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should connect biological insights to algorithmic or architectural strategies for energy-constrained computing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resource ceiling (per-topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no larger than $1.5M per year for five years and fund no more than six faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget proposals should generally stay within the stated annual and duration caps; exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective (Topic 4: Biology the Builder)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elucidate the fundamentally conserved rules of biological assembly of structural multifunctional materials with extreme mechanical properties and understand how these rules have been tuned through evolutionary processes across species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target discovery of conserved assembly rules and evolutionary tuning across species and articulate how the proposed work accomplishes this objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area (Topic 4): comparative assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative assessment of extreme structural materials (e.g. bone, shell, exoskeleton) across species that display similar functionality/adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative, cross-species studies that identify common principles or divergent solutions are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area (Topic 4): cellular energetics and forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental assessment of the cellular energetics, resources, and physical forces (mechanical, electrical, thermal) that determine form and rate of biological material assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experiments and/or models quantifying energetics and force-related determinants of assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area (Topic 4): identification of conserved proteins/molecules
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of novel and/or conserved proteins/molecules used in structural assembly, born out of evolutionary pressure, that enabled species survival in unique environments (biomineralization, scaffold construction, materials assembly, material degradation/recycling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include approaches to identify molecular components and assess their evolutionary conservation and functional roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area (Topic 4): methods to track materials creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel methods that combine molecular recognition and biotechnology modification of living systems to track materials creation at the molecular and macroscale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose innovative imaging/labeling/biotech tools to observe material synthesis across scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area (Topic 4): informed models of assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of informed models describing the process of structural material assembly at the molecular level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should be grounded in experimental data and predict assembly pathways or outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area (Topic 4): demonstration of rules-based synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration of 'rules' based synthesis of hybrid composite materials by synthetic and/or living systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include proof-of-concept demonstrations that apply discovered rules to synthesize materials with target properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI participation encouragement and additional funds (Topic 4 & others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 4 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; however, HBCU/MI participation is not a requirement. Applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including eligible HBCU/MI team members may make the proposal eligible for additional funding; eligibility is defined in Section I of the solicitation and teams should follow that guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective (Topic 5: Soft robotics control theory)
rubrics_metrics.description: This MURI topic seeks a novel mathematical data-driven and model-based control and systems theory framework designed for soft robotics that is amenable to reduced order modeling, uncertainty quantification and propagation and mathematical guarantees for control systems requirements of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must produce frameworks suitable for reduced-order modeling, UQ, and provable performance guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider robustness, safety, observability, controllability, complexity (Topic 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues such as robustness to uncertainty, and formal safety, ideas of observability/controllability, inverse kinematics, and stabilizability/detectability, should also be considered in the mathematical framework with attention to articulation of complexity in computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly address these control-theoretic properties and computational complexity in proposed models and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area (Topic 5): multidisciplinary contributions and fields
rubrics_metrics.description: This topic requires multidisciplinary participation of experts in control theory, robotics, material science, and computational science. Contributions from control theory, partial differential equations modeling, applied differential geometry, applied topology, materials science, reduced order modeling, uncertainty quantification, dynamical systems theory, nonequilibrium thermodynamics, and continuum, solid and structural mechanics, are anticipated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble teams spanning the listed disciplines and justify how contributions from each area will advance the research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research directions (Topic 5): modeling, UQ, geometric inverse kinematics, proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research directions include: (1) formulate a mathematical modeling framework for general soft robotics that is amenable to control theory and analysis; (2) provide a rigorous framework for uncertainty quantification and state and parameter estimation; (3) provide a geometric theory of inverse kinematics analogous to that of traditional robotics; (4) provide formal and rigorous proofs of these systems behaviors backed up with experimental results including the interrelationships between sensing, actuation and locomotion of robotic modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address one or more of these directions with both theoretical rigor and experimental validation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for environmental parameter considerations (Topic 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference will be given to proposals for which the possible changes in material parameters (i.e., internal variables) induced by the environment are also considered in the approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include analyses or experiments showing how environmental conditions alter material parameters and control performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective (Topic 6: non-reciprocal quantum materials & tunable superconducting diodes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals: 1) discover and explore novel, unconventional order parameters in quantum materials to concurrently break time-reversal and inversion symmetry, and 2) modulate these order parameters for tunability of Josephson diodes without external magnetic fields, to produce unprecedented high frequency functionalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on discovering order parameters and methods to tune them to achieve diode-like superconducting behavior without external magnetic fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration areas (Topic 6): explore mechanisms, diagnostics, models
rubrics_metrics.description: Research areas include: (1) discover and exploit unconventional order parameters to tune the superconducting diode effect; (2) elucidate fundamental mechanisms and limits for the origins of nonreciprocity, ideally under zero magnetic field; (3) apply or develop diagnostics to probe and verify underlying mechanisms; (4) develop physics-based methods to model and exploit high frequency dynamics and functionalities in tunable Josephson diodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine theoretical, computational, diagnostic and experimental work to address mechanisms and tunability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resource ceiling and exceptions (general across topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under these topics will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting up to a stated number of faculty researchers (varies by topic). Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chief(s) during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget within stated ceilings or proactively discuss justified exceptions with topic chiefs during white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exclusion (Topic 7): hardware-fidelity-only proposals not of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Simply improving hardware, e.g., the fidelity of N-qubit gates, is not of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must go beyond incremental hardware fidelity improvements and instead investigate fundamental potential, costs, and tradeoffs of N-qubit gates for algorithms, protocols, error correction, and related systems-level questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective (Topic 7: N-qubit gates)
rubrics_metrics.description: This topic seeks a deep and thorough basic research investigation of the fundamental potential, costs, and tradeoffs brought by N-qubit gates for advancements in quantum algorithms and protocols, including for quantum error correction, fault-tolerant quantum information processing, and quantum networking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should analyze algorithmic and protocol-level impacts, tradeoffs, and scaling of N-qubit gates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration areas (Topic 7): algorithms, implementations, limitations, characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas include: (1) novel or more efficient quantum algorithms and protocols enabled by N-qubit gates; (2) exploration of unconventional N-qubit gate implementations (e.g., qudits, native phenomena such as many-body interactions, etc.); (3) analysis of advantages, fundamental limitations, scalability and operational costs of N-qubit gate algorithms and protocols as compared to sequences decomposed into single and two-qubit gates; (4) understanding of noise channels and error budgets; (5) methods to characterize, verify, and validate N-qubit gate approaches; (6) experiments that can demonstrate or enhance theoretical insight early on. Approaches should be scalable with N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address both theoretical and experimental characterization, and demonstrate scalability beyond N=3 where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources (Topic 7 specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 5 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and team size should reflect the stated support limits unless exceptions are discussed with topic chiefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective (Topic 8: hot solid-state qubits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover, design and demonstrate new Josephson junction and gated-defined quantum dot based qubits compatible with operation at temperatures in the regime 300 mK to 1 K, whilst maintaining low error-rate quantum operations (i.e., < 1% error for a universal set of qubit operations). Qubits should be capable of running long sequences of gates without interference from initialization or reset requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target specified temperature regime and demonstrate or project <1% error for a universal gate set and long-sequence operation feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration areas (Topic 8): materials, designs, environment, theory, control, sympathetic cooling
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested areas: (1) study, design and fabrication of unconventional materials suitable for Josephson junction circuits or gate-defined quantum dot qubit operation at higher operational temperatures; (2) development of novel qubit designs with desirable energy-level structures to enable low-error rate reset methods; (3) engineering of the qubit environment to reduce thermally-coupled noise; (4) associated theory including modeling of thermally-induced material loss mechanisms, device thermalization, non-linearities at high temperatures and limits of active and initialization techniques; (5) development of optimized control techniques for active reset, initialization and readout with minimal side-effects; (6) methods analogous to sympathetic cooling with mixed species solid-state qubits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address materials, device physics, thermal modeling, and control strategies; consider sympathetic or selective cooling approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active initialization cases to consider (Topic 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should consider the following cases when developing new active initialization techniques: a) prior to running a quantum algorithm, rapidly remove excess thermal excitations and initialize the quantum states with low error; b) while running a quantum algorithm, active initialization or reset may be required while maintaining low operational error during the calculation; c) 'selective cooling' where in multi-qubit devices this approach would initialize specific data qubits while not affecting neighboring qubits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluate initialization/reset techniques appropriate for each case, and discuss impacts on neighboring qubits and algorithm execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources (Topic 8 specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting 5 or less faculty researchers and their associated students, postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure team and budget to fit within this support envelope or discuss exceptions with topic chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective (Topic 9: Quantum machine learning for quantum data)
rubrics_metrics.description: To develop and explore novel QML approaches to process quantum data, and to enable enhancements over the currently best quantum and classical methods. Specifically we envision exploiting quantum sensor data to avoid QRAM complications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on processing quantum sensor data and clarifying where QML offers advantages relative to classical ML, including costs of quantization and QRAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration areas (Topic 9): data suitability, platform innovation, comparisons, data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested areas: (1) fundamental analysis of the types of data best suited for QML, collected from various quantum sensors; (2) fundamental analysis of and innovations in QML platforms and their optimization for quantum sensing applications; (3) methods for comparing fundamental operations in quantum and classical ML realms and their limitations; (4) optimal methods of collecting either static or time dependent data amenable for QML processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address data-structure suitability, platform design, comparative analyses, and data acquisition methods that enable or demonstrate QML advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources (Topic 9 specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets and team sizes consistent with the stated caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-level contact and white paper consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chief(s) during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage topic chiefs early (contact information provided per topic) to discuss scope, exceptions, and fit prior to full proposal submission.
